attributes.scope: MEASUREMENT lane (read-only on memory_graph; owns tools/gdl/regression_set.py + its data file): build the FROZEN REGRESSION SET that answers 'is the graph genuinely useful' empirically. (1) SELECT ~24 STRICT-matched functions (source-matched, NOT webfrank-pinned) across >=8 TUs and >=4 mechanism families and >=3 eras of the campaign; for each, locate via git history the PRE-MATCH source state (the real starting point) and the matching commit; freeze the list (fn, TU, pre commit, post commit, mechanism family) in a committed manifest. (2) HARNESS: a script that, in an isolated worktree, reverts ONE function to its pre-match state and verifies the baseline residual reproduces; trial protocol doc: an agent is pointed at the function with a fixed budget, in arm A with full gdlmem access, in arm B with gdlmem queries forbidden (prompt-level) — outcome = reached-exact yes/no + probe count + build count. (3) PILOT: run 4 functions x both arms yourself by SIMULATING the agent's retrieval step only (cheap proxy: for each fn, does `brief`+`context`+`laws --residual` surface the mechanism that ACTUALLY closed it, per its matching commit? score retrieval hit/miss + rank) — full agent trials are a future run's budget decision, record the protocol for them. Deliverables: manifest, harness, retrieval-pilot numbers, methodology record w/ falsifier. No memory_graph code edits; no source edits outside the harness worktree; parallel fleets please pick other TUs
